changes.label: fig:frontier
changes.before: Accuracy and computation time on 379 independent input trajectories. Voltage RMSE is pooled over a common $1\ms$ observation grid after excluding reference spikes within $\pm10\ms$. DBNN, TCN, Branch-ELM, and LSTM use $1\ms$ input/output sampling. NEURON, CoreNEURON, and Neuron\_Reduce use a $0.5\ms$ integration step. Time is the sum of the median of three prepared, complete, single-trajectory computation calls per input. Measurements use a shared server with declared CPU affinity and GPU synchronization. The indicated ratio compares the displayed NEURON and DBNN GPU operating points.
changes.after: Voltage RMSE and prepared computation time on 379 independent inputs. RMSE pools $1\ms$ samples outside $\pm10\ms$ of reference spikes. Learned models sample at $1\ms$; numerical solvers integrate at $0.5\ms$. Time sums per-input medians of three complete single-trajectory calls on a shared server (Section~\ref{sec:metrics}).

changes.label: fig:order
changes.before: Interaction coefficients and error orders for two E--I input cases. Blue denotes dynamic inputs and green denotes constant inputs throughout. (a) Exponential capacitance-scaled E/I conductances with peaks $0.02\,\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ and decay times $2/5\ms$: the blue curve $\widehat\kappa_{EI}(t)$ is fitted across nine small-strength combinations. The gray dashed line is this dynamic case's best fixed coefficient $c^*_{EI}=0.0897712\,\mathrm{mV}^{-1}$ over $300\ms$; only the first $60\ms$ is displayed. (b) The capacitance-scaled conductances are held at $\gamma_E=\gamma_I=0.005\,\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ and voltage is observed at equilibrium. The analytical second-order coefficient $\kappa_{EI}=0.0857143\,\mathrm{mV}^{-1}$ equals the exact fixed coefficient, so both coincide on the green line. (c) Pair-interaction RMSE for the same two cases. Fitted slopes over the shaded range $\varepsilon\in[10^{-3},10^{-2}]$ are 1.99975 and 2.99912, respectively.
changes.after: Interaction coefficients and pairwise approximation errors for dynamic (blue) and constant (green) E--I inputs. (a) Regression-fitted $\widehat\kappa_{EI}(t)$ for exponential conductances and the best fixed coefficient $c^*_{EI}$ over $300\ms$; only the first $60\ms$ is shown. (b) Equilibrium for constant $\gamma_E=\gamma_I=0.005\,\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$, where $\kappa_{EI}=c^*_{EI}$. (c) Pair-interaction RMSE versus the common strength $\varepsilon$; shading marks the slope-fitting interval $[10^{-3},10^{-2}]$.

changes.label: fig:finite
changes.before: Quadratic corrections at biologically motivated response scales. Shading marks the EPSP band $0.2$--$6\mV$, motivated by \cite{li2014,li2019}; all displayed IPSP magnitudes are at most $3\mV$. Horizontal dotted lines mark the 5\% relative RMS tolerance on the joint above-background response. (a)--(b) Passive controls with fixed first-order kernels and quadratic readouts, fitted to second-order targets and held fixed over the strength sweep. (c) Mouse L5PC with its original active channels: 28 held-out subthreshold responses from proximal and distributed inputs. Dashed curves sum complete isolated E/I responses; solid curves add a fixed bilinear correction. Shapes identify spatial groups. Appendix~\ref{app:finite} gives the input parameters and integration-step controls.
changes.after: Relative RMS error at biologically motivated response amplitudes. Shading marks the $0.2$--$6\mV$ EPSP band \cite{li2014,li2019}; horizontal dotted lines mark 5\% error relative to the joint above-background response. (a)--(b) Passive synchronous and tonic inputs with fixed quadratic readouts fitted to second-order responses. (c) Active mouse L5PC: 28 held-out proximal and distributed inputs. Dashed curves sum complete isolated E/I responses; solid curves add a fixed bilinear correction.
